Linh T.: quick RFC follow-up — proposal to slim down the decision surface for automatic rollbacks. Problem: too many noisy signals -> rollbacks flapping; we should converge on a compact, composable surface that we can reason about and test. pinging eng-runtime, oncall, product. 
Maya P.: sounds good. which signals are you planning to keep? error-rate + latency right? any model-quality metrics? :thinking_face: 
Alex R.: minimal set i'd push for: 1) request error rate (5xx/timeout), 2) p95 latency, 3) model-quality regression flag (from evals), 4) infra OOMs/GPUs failed. Everything else should be advisory. Keep the automatic trigger simple. 
Linh T.: agreed. here's the sketch: central aggregator computes a "circuit score" S = w1*err + w2*norm(p95) + w3*qual_regress + w4*infra_faults. thresholds: S > 0.7 -> pause canary; S in (0.5,0.7) -> throttle traffic; smoothing: exponential window 90s, min 3 samples. 
ops-bot: metrics snapshot for canary/1234: err=0.012, p95=220ms, infra_faults=0, qual_regress=false. (sample rate 1%)
Alex R.: can we see the normalization and weights? also how does smoothing interact with short spikes during rollout? 
Linh T.: proposed default weights {"err":0.5, "p95":0.25, "qual":0.2, "infra":0.05}. norm(p95) = min(1, (p95-150)/350). smoothing alpha=0.3 (exp), hold window 60s post-trigger to avoid flip-flop. 
Frank O.: central aggregator is a nice concept but raises single-point concerns. if aggregator hiccups we lose rollbacks entirely. can we make it hybrid? local proxies compute a local S_local and aggregator computes S_global — trigger fires only if both exceed thresholds or if global alone is above a hard cutoff. 
Sasha K.: hybrid seems safe. also we should separate advisory signals (debug-only) from trigger signals at the contract level. metadata contract idea: each signal includes {"name", "type": "trigger|advisory", "confidence", "sample_rate", "schema_version"}. That makes testing and evolution easier. 
Maya P.: important: product metrics (user-visible quality) are slow to compute. we'll need a lag-tolerant path: model-quality regressions -> advisory fast path for humans, automatic only if coupled with infra/latency signals. 
Linh T.: agreed — automatic triggers will never fire on quality-regress alone. plan: implement v1 central aggregator + local proxies as fallback, add schema for signals and enforce contract in ingestion. we'll run a 2-week shadow run before enabling automated actions. 
Alex R.: can you paste the example ingestion contract/schema? i want to add it to the RFC. 
Linh T.: ```json
{"signal_name":"p95_latency_ms","type":"trigger","value":220.0,"confidence":0.98,"sample_rate":0.01,"schema_version":"1"}
``` 
Maya P.: questions about ops: how do we instrument sample rates to avoid cost explosion for embeddings/quality checks? 
ops-bot: note: quality checks currently sampled at 0.5% for live canaries; we can route full evals to dedicated job if needed. 
Sasha K.: also propose a lightweight test harness: replay the last 30m of traffic through aggregator in 'what-if' mode to validate thresholds. makes rollbacks auditable. 
Frank O.: will we expose the circuit score and its components in console? we need explainability when oncall gets paged. 
Linh T.: yes — expose S and breakdown, raw signals, and the smoothing window UI. also include a 'why-paused' event with pointers to contributing signals. 
Maya P.: LGTM. next steps? 
Linh T.: action items: 1) Linh + Alex implement aggregator prototype (2 wks). 2) Sasha build signal schema + test harness (1w). 3) Ops (Frank) add local proxy fallback plan + runbook (1w). 4) Product + oncall run shadow for 2 weeks. I'll open a PR with proto config and rollout checklist. 
deploy-bot: Canary 1234: traffic ramp paused at 50% due to circuit_score=0.76 (>0.7). Automated pause recorded. 
Alex R.: nice, that pause proves the wiring works in shadow. please include link to playbook in the PR. :thumbsup:
